verdict.rationale: Slate documents spawning agents that run in the background while you keep working, queuing tasks, and bypassing permission prompts with --yolo, so one-off autonomous background work is first-party. However, these are ad-hoc tasks started inside an interactive session, not set-up automations. Nothing shows recurring schedules, event triggers, or headless runs, so a one-off background run is not treated as a standing automation. missing for 10: scheduled/recurring automations, event-triggered runs, headless/unattended execution outside an interactive session, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: While one or more agents run in the background, you can keep talking with Slate: plan next steps, queue up additional tasks, or spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once.
We support `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (alias: `--yolo`) to bypass permission prompts.
`goal` and `deep-research` are built-in programs. They are user-visible workflows
